To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) classical hand-designed controllers excel at solving the stabilization task in-distribution but fail at out-of-distribution, 2) neural network policies can be trained to generalize across density settings and 3) Flow provides a flexible platform for developing and benchmarking traffic controllers.

1) Flow is a novel computational framework that enables the use of deep reinforcement learning for traffic control; 2) Flow enables easy benchmarking of classical (hand-designed) traffic controllers with learned policies; and 3) Flow can be used to develop reliable controllers that can solve complex tasks, such as controlling autonomous vehicles in the mixed-autonomy traffic in a ring road, across a range of densities.

(i) hand-designed controllers are not robust to changes in the distribution of the traffic; (ii) deep RL methods can be used to develop reliable controllers; and (iii) deep RL controllers generalize to out-of-sample traffic conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
two aspects: (i) developing new computational tools for RL in traffic, and (ii) using those tools to develop reliable traffic control policies.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

we have developed an RL framework for autonomous traffic control, which enables the use of deep RL methods such as Policy Gradient for traffic control and benchmarking the performance with classical (including hand-design) controllers.
Flow enables the design of reliable controllers for complex nonlinear traffic dynamics and enables the benchmarking of learned controllers with hand-designed ones.

we are able to show that neural network policies can learn to stabilize mixed-autonomy traffic, even in the presence of out-of-distribution conditions, and that they can generalize to different network configurations and vehicle dynamics, and we are able to compare their performance with hand-designed controllers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide a novel framework that enables RL for traffic control and benchmarking the performance between RL and classical controllers.
Flow provides a platform for benchmarking and comparing different controllers in traffic, including hand-designed controllers and learned policies.

we have developed a framework to support the design, implementation, benchmarking, and deployment of RL methods for traffic control, and we demonstrate its utility by solving a complex traffic control problem using RL.
The main takeaway from our work is that
deep RL can solve complex traffic control tasks that are hard to solve with hand-designed controllers, and can generalize to out-of-sample settings.
RL can solve complex traffic tasks, and that Flow is a useful tool to develop reliable controllers and benchmark the performance of classical controllers.
RL is a promising direction to develop robust controllers for autonomous vehicles, especially when the dynamics of traffic are highly complex.
